resources.string: Mirror any app with a horizontal flip for HUD / windscreen use. Unlike classic overlay mirrors, player controls stay usable: the picture is visual-only, and a floating button can hide or show it instantly.
In the system sheet choose a single app (not Entire screen), then open the player. Use the floating button to hide or show the mirrored overlay.
Allow Mirra to display over other apps first.
Overlay shown — taps go through to the app.
Overlay hidden — interact with the player directly.
Required for the mirrored overlay and the floating toggle.
Shows a persistent control to hide, show, or stop the mirror.
Recommended. Lets the overlay be fully opaque (no ghost of the original picture) while taps still reach the player.
Turn on Mirra in Accessibility so the flipped picture fully covers the original. Without it Android may show both images at once, or block pass-through taps.

Lets Mirra draw a trusted HUD overlay so the mirrored picture does not swallow player taps. Can also inject remapped gestures when “Mirrored taps” is enabled. Mirra does not read your screen content or type text.
Controls for the HUD overlay while it is running.
Overlay visible. Taps pass through to the player.
Overlay hidden. Player is fully interactive.
Corrects the image for a windscreen reflection.
Useful for some projector / HUD mounts.
Use when the phone is mounted upside down.
Hide the status and navigation bars in the overlay.
The overlay is visual only. Play, pause and seek still hit the real player.
Tap where a control appears on the flipped picture. Requires Accessibility.
Enable Accessibility to use mirrored taps
Draggable button over other apps. Tap to hide/show, long-press for actions.
Prevents sleep while the overlay is visible.

Grant overlay permission. Notifications are optional. Accessibility is strongly recommended: it lets Mirra draw a fully opaque flipped picture that still passes taps. Without it Android may either ghost the original app underneath or block pass-through taps.
Tap Start mirror. In the system dialog choose a single app — never Entire screen, or the overlay will film itself. Then open the player, maps, or whatever you want on the HUD.
A bubble stays on top of every app. Tap it to hide the mirrored picture and use the player normally, tap again to bring the HUD image back. Drag it to the edge. Long-press for flip / stop.

Pass-through (default) does not eat touches: pause, seek and buttons of the app underneath keep working while you still see the flipped overlay. If you want to tap the controls where they appear after the flip, enable Mirrored taps (Accessibility).
Place the phone facing the windscreen. Horizontal flip makes the reflection readable. Keep screen on is recommended. Dim the overlay if the glass is too bright.
Android 14 QPR2 or later. Single-app screen sharing is a platform feature. This is version 0.1.0 and is not published on Play / RuStore yet.
